verdict: READY TO MERGE - 13 of 13 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: _timed_hook puts a hard subprocess timeout on the hook, so a reintroduced backtracking scan fails one test fast instead of hanging the whole suite.
test_long_token_does_not_hide_a_real_plan_path is a good negative control: a skipped oversized token must not mask a real plan path later in the same command.
test_bash_path_token_shapes_still_validate covers bare, single-quoted, double-quoted-with-pipe and relative path shapes against the new quote-aware token split, end to end through the real hook.
test_run_git_timeout_surfaces_as_oserror checks the real exception translation in run_git (TimeoutExpired to TimeoutError, an OSError), which the existing OSError handlers depend on.

The backtracking `[^\s'"]*<dir>[/\\][^\s'"]+?\.json` findall is replaced by a whitespace/quote split plus str.find/rfind scanning. This removes the quadratic-or-worse stall on long whitespace-free tokens, and the 4096-char cap bounds the per-token cost.

The new scanner splits adjacent paths in one token into separate candidates, e.g. 'docs/PLANS/a.json,docs/PLANS/b.json'. The old greedy prefix merged them into a single non-existent path, so this also improves detection.

run_git centralizes stdin=DEVNULL and a bounded wait, and maps TimeoutExpired to TimeoutError (an OSError subclass). The existing `except OSError` paths in main_worktree and _activate_project absorb a hung git without new handlers.
Every git lookup in project.py and config.py now routes through run_git, and tests/lib/test_project.py adds a parametrized guard that checks this, so a future direct subprocess.run is caught.

Plan decisions D11-D15 record every change from the frozen spec (path syntax, dedup, probes for each folder, checkout anchoring, J1-J4 baselines), each tied to a review ID, so the spec stays frozen and the plan holds the current design.

All plan anchors other than TASK-5's resolve at head: writing_docstrings_api.py:25/281/302, writing_docstrings_models.py:59, docstring_tiers.py:44, test_root_separation.py:206, SKILL.md:25/38, contract.ts:123, README.md:28 and strap.py:550. Every regression command it names points to a test file that exists.
The spec's anti-goals (no -in from restyle words, never two -p agents on one file) are concrete, testable failures, and plan D11's dedup on resolved paths enforces the second.

The runner agent change closes a real hole (a session-role scenario stopping before record-run). It matches strap-skills SKILL.md:110 and does not trip the init-before-record pin in test_strap_agents_contract.py:70-75.

The Bash target scan swaps a backtracking regex, which went quadratic on long whitespace-free tokens, for whitespace and quote splitting plus str.find/rfind, with a 4096-char token cap. Quoted, piped and absolute path shapes still validate.

The regression tests run the real hook as a subprocess with a hard 15s timeout, so a stall fails fast instead of hanging the suite. A 200k-char token placed next to a real invalid plan path still blocks.
run_git puts stdin=DEVNULL and a bounded wait in one helper and turns TimeoutExpired into an OSError subclass, so the existing `except OSError` handlers keep working unchanged.
Plan 0004 records each review-driven departure from the spec as decisions D11-D15 with rationale and leaves the frozen spec untouched. Its freeze digest matches the plan content at head.
The strap-scenario-runner rule now states that a scenario ending at a dispatch still runs record-run, which closes the gap that let session-role runs skip the record.
The harness plugin version moves 0.51.0 -> 0.51.1 for the hook, lib and agent changes, as the Releases rule requires.

critical.name: test_run_git_closes_stdin_and_bounds_the_wait is a mock-wiring test
critical.summary:
The test replaces subprocess.run with a recorder and asserts only that the stub received stdin=DEVNULL and a positive timeout. run_git does nothing but forward those keyword arguments, so the test restates the implementation's call shape: it cannot show that a child is actually detached from the caller's stdin or actually killed after the bound. A refactor that passes stdin through a different route (for example Popen plus communicate) breaks the test even though behavior holds. A refactor that keeps the kwargs but loses the effect passes it. Under the brief's test-design rule, a stub-then-assert-the-stub-call test is neither behavioral nor integration.

Also (overall): The test swaps `subprocess.run` for a recorder and asserts that `run_git` passed `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` and a positive `timeout`. It checks the call's kwargs, not behavior: it never shows that a child sees EOF on stdin or that a slow child is cut off. Under the project's test-design rule this is neither behavioral nor integration.
fix: Convert to behavioral tests that run real children through run_git. Stdin: start a child interpreter with stdin=subprocess.PIPE that is never written or closed, have it call run_git([sys.executable, '-c', 'import sys; sys.stdin.read()']) (or git hash-object --stdin), and assert that it finishes within a short timeout. Without DEVNULL the grandchild blocks on the open pipe. Timeout: monkeypatch project_module._GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to 0.5 and assert that run_git([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(10)']) raises TimeoutError within a couple of seconds.
Delete the test and keep test_run_git_timeout_surfaces_as_oserror plus the behavioral replacement above as the only run_git coverage.

Make it behavioral: point fd 0 at an open pipe (`r, w = os.pipe(); saved = os.dup(0); os.dup2(r, 0)`, restore in `finally`), monkeypatch `project_module._GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to 2, run `run_git([sys.executable, '-c', 'import sys; print(repr(sys.stdin.read()))'])` and assert stdout is `''`. An inherited stdin blocks on the open pipe and times out, so the test fails.

Add a real-child timeout case: monkeypatch `_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to 1, run `run_git([sys.executable, '-c', 'import time; time.sleep(30)'])` and assert `TimeoutError`. Then delete the kwargs-recording test.

critical.name: test_every_git_lookup_goes_through_run_git asserts stub call kwargs, not routing or behavior
critical.summary:
Each parametrized caller (_git_toplevel, main_worktree, config._origin_head) runs against a recorder that replaces the global subprocess.run, and the test then checks the recorded kwargs. That is a mock-chain wiring test under the brief's rule. Its name also claims more than it checks: the patch targets the shared subprocess module, so a caller that calls subprocess.run directly with its own stdin/timeout kwargs passes, and nothing proves the call goes through run_git. A call missing the kwargs fails with a bare KeyError on c['stdin'] rather than an assertion message.

Also (overall): The test stubs `subprocess.run`, calls `_git_toplevel`, `main_worktree` and `_origin_head`, and asserts only that the stub received `stdin=DEVNULL` and `timeout>0`. That is routing verification through a stub, not behavior. Its name also claims every git lookup, yet `branch_capture.py:41`, `plan_checks.py:237` and `todo_sync/scaffold.py:96` still call git through `subprocess.run` directly.
fix: Convert to a behavioral test with a fake git executable: put a git (git.cmd on Windows, a shell script elsewhere) on a tmp PATH that sleeps, or that blocks reading stdin. Monkeypatch project_module._GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to a small value, then assert that each caller returns or raises promptly (_git_toplevel and _origin_head raise OSError, main_worktree returns the start path). Mark the test cross_os if it depends on the launcher shape.

If a wiring check is kept anyway, rename it to state what it checks (every subprocess call from these lookups closes stdin and sets a timeout), use c.get('stdin') and c.get('timeout') so a missing kwarg fails as an assertion, and pair it with the behavioral test above.

Make it behavioral: put a fake `git` on PATH that sleeps (POSIX shim, `skipif` on win32), monkeypatch `project_module._GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to 1, then assert that `main_worktree(root)` returns `root.resolve()`, that `project_root(root)` raises `TimeoutError`, and that `cfg.resolve_base_branch()` behaves as specified.

Replace it with a contract test that parses `harness_lib/project.py` and `harness_lib/config.py` and fails on any `subprocess.run` call outside `run_git`. Name it for the lookups it covers, not 'every'.

Also (overall): TASK-5 anchors `plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3` on `"version": "0.51.0",`, but this PR bumps that line to 0.51.1. `plan.py check 0004` runs `anchor_problems` (plugins/harness/scripts/plan.py:213) and at the PR head reports: anchor TASK-5 plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3: '"version": "0.51.0",' not found; line 3 reads '"version": "0.51.1",'. The plan therefore merges already failing its own check. Changing an anchor on a frozen plan needs a refreeze. Related: `frozen.commit` 0755ef6 (and the PIP 'Frozen ... at 0755ef6' line) names a commit that is not in this PR's history (577f516..c857744 holds e5e97ea, not 0755ef6). The digest still matches the content, so only the commit pointer is foreign to the branch.
fix: Change the TASK-5 anchor expect to `"version": "0.51.1",` through the plan driver, refreeze plan 0004 (developer OK, routine) and re-render the PIP so line 189 matches.
Or drop the version-line anchor from TASK-5 (the bump target 0.52.0 does not depend on the old value), then refreeze and re-render.
Through the plan driver, set the TASK-5 anchor expect to `"version": "0.51.1",`, refreeze plan 0004 on this branch (so frozen.commit is a commit in this history), then re-render the PIP.
Land the plan docs on the 1117-writing-docstrings branch instead and refreeze there after this PR merges, so the anchor is taken against the 0.51.1 line.

important.name: Stall test never reaches the per-token target scan; the length cap and _next_json_end are unpinned
important.summary:
In all three blobs the huge token has no '.json' (the only '.json' sits in the separate token 'out.json'), and every blob exceeds _MAX_TOKEN_CHARS. So _bash_target_tokens drops the huge token before _token_targets runs, and the 'plain' case exits even earlier at the stdlib pre-check because it names no plan directory. The docstring ('holding a plan directory, .json and one huge whitespace-free token ... the target scan is linear in the command, not quadratic or worse in a token') does not match what runs. Removing the 4096 cap still passes all three cases, because the '.json' filter alone skips them. Yet without the cap, _next_json_end rescans pos..end with rfind for every '.json' occurrence, which is quadratic for a token like 'docs/PLANS/' + 'a.json' * 40000. The test guards the old regex, but not the new code's load-bearing cap.

Also (runtime): All three blobs in test_long_whitespace_free_token_does_not_stall_the_hook (200k chars) and the long token in test_long_token_does_not_hide_a_real_plan_path are longer than _MAX_TOKEN_CHARS (4096). _bash_target_tokens drops them at line 133 before _token_targets/_next_json_end runs. The test docstring says 'the target scan is linear in the command', but the scan never runs on those inputs. If the scanner regressed (for example, a backtracking regex reintroduced inside _token_targets), these tests would still pass. The scanner's worst case is a token just under the cap with many '.json' occurrences and directory prefixes, and no test covers it.

Also (overall): The command `echo aaaa... > out.json` names no plan or review directory, so `_cannot_target` (validate_pr_json_schema.py:372-377) returns True and the hook exits before config load and before `_bash_target_tokens`. The case passes against the old backtracking regex too, so it cannot catch a regression. It also contradicts the test docstring, which says every case holds a plan directory. All three cases also lack `.json` in the long token, so `_MAX_TOKEN_CHARS` and the `.json` membership guard both skip the token, and none of them runs the new `_token_targets` scan on a long input.
fix: Add blobs whose huge token itself carries a directory prefix and '.json', for example 'docs/PLANS/' + 'a.json' * 40_000 (ids 'many-json-hits') and 'docs/PLANS/' * 20_000 + 'x.json' (ids 'dir-run-then-json'), so the cap, or a truly linear scan, is what keeps the hook under _SLOW_HOOK_SECONDS.
Change the docstring to describe what the cases cover, and drop or rename the 'plain' case, since it tests only the pre-check.

Add a parametrized case with a token just under the cap that holds many '.json' and 'docs/PLANS/' occurrences (e.g. `('docs/PLANS/x' + '.json') * 250`, trimmed under 4096 chars), and keep the 15-second _timed_hook bound.
Reword the test docstring to say the length cap skips the huge token, and add a separate scanner-focused case.

Change the command to `f"echo {blob} > docs/PLANS/out.json"` so every case passes the pre-check and reaches the scanner, and add a case whose long token (at or under 4096 chars) contains `docs/PLANS/` and repeated `.json`, so the str-search loop itself is timed.

minor.name: _next_json_end searches the whole token when .json sits at offset 0
minor.summary:
_next_json_end calls norm.rfind(prefix, pos, end - 1). When a token starts with '.json' (pos 0, end 0) the slice end is -1, which Python reads as 'up to the last character', so rfind scans the whole token and finds any directory prefix that comes AFTER the '.json'. For a token such as '.json,docs/PLANS/a.json' the scanner emits the spurious candidate '.json' (token[0:5]) before the real one. That breaks the docstring contract 'the first .json ... that follows a directory prefix'. The real path is still found and _target_kind filters out the stray '.json' later, so the visible impact is one wasted is_file probe. Still, the guard depends on a negative-index accident.

Also (overall): `_dir_prefixes` rebuilds `rel.replace('\\', '/').strip('/') + '/'`, which is `_rel_token(rel)` (line 65-67) without the leading slash. Two copies of the directory normalization can drift apart.
fix: Clamp the slice end: `norm.rfind(prefix, pos, max(end - 1, pos))`, so an empty slice returns -1.

Or rewrite the scan so it is linear and has no negative index: compute `threshold = min(norm.find(p, pos) + len(p) for p in prefixes if norm.find(p, pos) >= 0)`, then `end = norm.find('.json', threshold + 1)`. That gives the same result without the per-occurrence rfind.
Return `[_rel_token(rel)[1:] for rel in (cfg.artifacts.plans, cfg.artifacts.reviews)]`.

minor.name: config.py now imports harness_lib.project at module top but keeps function-local imports of it

Or keep the deferred style and move the run_git import inside _origin_head to match.
Change line 16 to `from harness_lib.project import main_worktree, project_root, run_git` and delete the imports at lines 213 and 234.

minor.name: run_git docstring overstates how callers handle a timeout
minor.summary: The docstring says a timeout raises TimeoutError, 'the failure callers already treat as "git unusable"'. Only `main_worktree` (project.py:56-59) and the hook's `_activate_project` catch OSError. `_git_toplevel`/`project_root` and `config._origin_head` (config.py:464-469) let it propagate, so a hung git in `resolve_base_branch` ends a driver with a traceback instead of falling back to `main`.
fix: Catch OSError in `_origin_head` and return None, so `resolve_base_branch` falls back as documented, and narrow the run_git docstring to the callers that handle it.
Reword the docstring to: callers that catch OSError (main_worktree, the hooks' project lookup) treat it as git unusable; others propagate it.
